overall_summary: Analysis of 35 Short videos shows strong channel performance for high-stakes planetary scenarios and atmospheric disruption concepts published during early morning (04:45-05:00 UTC) and midday (12:00-12:15 UTC) slots. The top performer 'What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn?' reached 1,041 studio views with 50.79% average view percentage, while 'What If Earth Lost Its Atmosphere for 5 Seconds?' generated the highest watch time (262 estimated minutes watched, 64.29% average view percentage). Retention drops rapidly after 20-25% progress on lower-performing titles, requiring tighter visual hooks and immediate visual transformations.

what_is_working.pattern: Catastrophic global reset scenarios with short time limits
what_is_working.evidence: 'What If Earth Lost Its Atmosphere for 5 Seconds?' achieved 881 Studio views, 262 estimated minutes watched, and a 64.29% average view percentage.
what_is_working.action: Produce content centered around brief, intense planetary physical changes (e.g., 5-second or instant disruptions).

what_is_working.evidence: 'What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn?' achieved 1,041 Studio views (50.79% view percentage) and 'What If Sound Could Travel Through Space?' reached 715 Studio views.
what_is_working.action: Focus on high-concept space science hypotheses paired with strong visual celestial transformations.

what_to_improve.pattern: Low engagement on abstract chemical or color shift visual changes
what_to_improve.evidence: 'What If Water Turned Into Liquid Mercury' (19 views), 'What If Earth's Atmosphere Turned Neon Pink' (29.93% view percentage), and 'What If All Sand Turned to Glass' (25 views) underperformed significantly.
what_to_improve.action: Avoid cosmetic visual shifts; ground hypothetical scenarios in extreme physical consequences and stakes.

what_to_improve.evidence: 'What If Earth Lost Its Magnetic Field?' had one upload get 365 views and the duplicate get only 10 views (1151% distorted view percentage).
what_to_improve.action: Ensure single clean uploads per topic to prevent algorithm split-testing issues.

retention_insights.evidence: 'What If Earth Lost Its Atmosphere for 5 Seconds?' maintained relative retention above 0.50 from progress 0.08 through 0.49, ending at 0.5384 relative retention.
retention_insights.action: Use step-by-step sequential impact pacing (0-2s visual hook, 3-10s immediate atmosphere loss, 10-25s global fallout, 25-35s scientific resolution).

retention_insights.drop_or_strength: Flat retention curve with high completion
retention_insights.evidence: 'What If All Lightning Struck At The Same Second?' maintained relative retention between 0.4852 and 0.4995 from progress 0.06 to 0.49, driving 53.55% average view percentage.
retention_insights.action: Maintain fast audio-visual pacing and rapid event escalation to prevent drop-off between 10% and 30% progress.

retention_insights.evidence: 'What If Saturn Replaced Our Moon?' dropped relative retention from 0.4361 at 1% progress to 0.0853 by 25% progress.
retention_insights.action: Deliver the core visual transformation within the first 3 seconds rather than building up slowly.

best_posting_windows.reason: Yielded the channel's highest view count video ('What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn?' - 1,041 views at 04:56 UTC) and high views on 'What If Sound Could Travel Through Space?' (715 views at 04:47 UTC).
Produced the highest watch time video ('What If Earth Lost Its Atmosphere for 5 Seconds?' - 881 views, 262 minutes watched at 12:08 UTC).
